I don't mean to be spiteful or emotional about anyone's business, but my experience here was extremely dissatisfying, a huge waste of time, and completely unacceptable. I felt like I was deceived. I'm happy to share my personal experience as a cautionary tale.

Time is precious. Don't play with patients' feelings, and you shouldn't make money by bullying patients' insecurities. If my child's teeth were already beautiful enough, why would they need further enhancements?

This incident occurred at a dental clinic that offers tooth enamel filler injections for cosmetic purposes. We chose this option because our child is afraid of pain and wanted to practice with the enhanced teeth before moving on to other techniques that require more careful dental care.

On our first visit, we waited a very long time. Today, we were still half an hour late. It felt like we didn't have an appointment; they couldn't keep to the scheduled time.

During our previous visit, the doctor showed us a model, and we agreed on a price of over 40,000 baht. We paid a deposit, and the doctor assured us that the procedure would be even better than the model because it would include polishing. We scheduled the actual procedure for today.

However, before the procedure, the clinic called to say that we would be seeing another doctor who is considered highly skilled, at a national level. We agreed and confirmed the appointment.

Today, the new doctor criticized my child's teeth multiple times. My daughter's teeth are very large, and I'm worried that if we do the injection method, they'll become even bigger and she won't be able to accept it after the procedure.

So I showed the new dentist a simulation from our previous dentist.
I said, "This is it. We're happy with this result."

The new dentist kept emphasizing that my daughter's teeth are large and I'm afraid she won't be able to accept the injection method.

I then asked to speak directly with the dentist, saying,
"Please, don't use words that reinforce my daughter's insecurities.
Just do the procedure as the previous dentist showed us. We're satisfied with that."

The dentist hesitated, making me wonder if their intention was to get veneers done.

I insisted that my daughter definitely wouldn't want any tooth grinding or gum separation; she's afraid of the pain. I asked them to do the injection method first.

The dentist said, "Then have the previous dentist do it." We said okay.

But the front desk staff said that we needed to schedule an appointment, but not for today, as that dentist isn't regularly available.

But we had a formal appointment with both the dentist and the staff the day before!

The person who seemed to be in charge said that the dentist had left the clinic.

So what's the truth? Is the dentist just not regularly available? But what about the appointment I had? Now they say the doctor has left.

The clinic offered to end the matter by returning my deposit.

I said okay, and I would write a review.

I'm still wondering why the clinic fired that doctor. He was a doctor who provided good information, was straightforward, and didn't hurt the patient's feelings like what I experienced today. Or are they just attracting customers with easy, inexpensive techniques, and then moving on to other techniques to achieve their goals? Otherwise, why would they change doctors who can't do the job?

During the exchange, several customers in the clinic overheard the sales pitch. I can say I'm not happy to recommend this clinic.

I'm not comfortable disclosing the clinic's real name here.

But I'm happy to share the details with close friends.

I'm not someone who's never had dental work done before; I've been doing it since I was young. My mouth is practically covered in dental work!

I know how important beautiful teeth are, and I'm very familiar with the procedures.

I'm not trying to harm or upset anyone with this, but I don't want my friends to fall for it.

I want the world to know that there are good clinics where people become close friends with the doctors.

I've also encountered bad clinics, and today I feel terrible.

Let me tell you, a big, luxurious building and numerous positive reviews don't guarantee that everything is good.

Today's story is about a mother who helped her child escape from

the world of illusion, where cheap media is used as a trap. When the customer didn't comply, they simply returned the deposit. But the memory, the customer's wasted time on this game for two days, the heartbreak – even after returning home, the child kept asking, "Mom, is my tooth really big and ugly?" How can these things be fixed or compensated for?
